pensamiento:
I'm going through the quality checks one by one: QUS-001 through QUS-005 all pass, since each has a clear role, a single atomic requirement, no unnecessary notes, a real benefit, and no imposed technology. I'm now starting on QUS-006, which looks ambiguous.

I'm checking QUS-006 more closely: the terms "mensual" and "mes seleccionado" don't say how the month gets selected, and it's unclear which accounts or what the PDF contains. Since no error cases are defined for a failed download, that one doesn't meet the requirement. I'm also confirming that QUS-007, QUS-008 and QUS-009 don't conflict with the other requirements.

I'm checking INV-003 next, and it's borderline: the story is reasonably clear, but it doesn't say which accounts are included, what the PDF should contain, which months can be selected, or how errors are handled. Since those scope details are missing, I'm leaning toward marking it as not meeting the requirement.

I'm checking INV-005 next: its two criteria are mostly observable, but the masking of the account number is vague since it doesn't say how many digits stay visible, and the requirement that the statement includes the month's movements doesn't define completeness or error cases.

I'm checking DOR-001 next: PDF generation likely depends on the core system for the movement data, and that dependency isn't mentioned, so it doesn't meet the requirement. DOR-002 also fails, since the available periods, the error case for an empty month, and the generation failure aren't defined. I'm now looking at DOR-003, wondering whether non-functional requirements apply, since that would only be the case for a critical feature or high volume.

I'm working through the BM checks now: BM-001 and BM-002 don't apply, since the download isn't a sensitive operation and doesn't touch the login session. BM-003 is covered because the account number appears masked. I'm checking whether the PDF gets stored on the device, which is what BM-004 depends on.

I'm going to treat BM-004 as passing, since the HU stores the PDF locally but nothing in it contradicts the security controls, and there's no evidence of a defect. Moving on, BM-005 doesn't apply because downloading a statement isn't a monetary operation or a data change, and I'm now checking BM-006 for whether the download button creates a new screen.

I'm weighing whether BM-006 counts as a defect: the story doesn't mention accessibility, and it's unclear whether the download adds a new screen. Since the team's default DoR isn't visible to me, I'm leaning toward flagging it as a minor gap, with a recommendation to mention accessibility.

I'm now checking BM-007: the story depends on the network to download the statement, and it doesn't define an error case for losing connection, so I'm marking it as a major gap. BM-008 doesn't apply, since the download doesn't rely on device-specific functions. For BM-009, the statement is personal financial data that gets shared with the user's own device, and I'm checking whether the purpose is stated.

I'm now looking at BM-009, and the statement is personal data shared with the user's own device, with its purpose stated, so that one passes. For BM-010, the statement is information given to the client, so the SUGEF criterion applies, and since the story doesn't mention validating it with Cumplimiento or any applicable rule, I'm leaning toward flagging it as a major gap.

Now I'm settling on the defect list: DOR-001, DOR-002, BM-007, BM-006 and BM-010, with INV-003 folded into the period and scope gaps. I'm leaning toward returning the story with a size estimate of 3.

I'm settling the last few checks: BAN-04 covers exporting a 12-month history to PDF while BAN-09 covers a single monthly statement, so they overlap in capability but serve different purposes and aren't duplicates. Since the QUS-008 role, action and benefit differ, I'm leaving it alone. I'll write the recommendations in Spanish, tied to the defects I've found, and keep personal data

recomendaciones.texto: Indicar de qué sistema o servicio se obtienen los movimientos y los datos del estado de cuenta (por ejemplo, el core bancario) y si la generación del PDF depende de un servicio o proveedor externo.
Definir las reglas: periodos mensuales disponibles para descargar (rango de meses), qué pasa si el mes no tiene movimientos, y el mensaje y comportamiento si la generación del PDF falla.
Aclarar el alcance: cómo se selecciona el mes, si la descarga aplica a una cuenta o a todas las cuentas del cliente, y qué datos incluye el PDF (saldo inicial y final, encabezado, etc.).
Agregar que la nueva opción de descarga cumple accesibilidad (lector de pantalla, contraste y tamaño de texto, referencia WCAG 2.1 AA), o indicar que la DoR del equipo lo incluye por defecto.

Definir el comportamiento sin conexión, con red lenta, con tiempo de espera agotado o con error del servicio durante la descarga, incluyendo si el cliente puede reintentar sin duplicar archivos o solicitudes.
Indicar la regla normativa SUGEF aplicable al estado de cuenta entregado al cliente o su validación con el área de Cumplimiento antes de pasar a la fábrica.

texto:
La HU BAN-09 quedó registrada como borrador con decisión **devolver** (estimación de 3 puntos). Una persona debe aprobar la revisión.

Hay seis defectos: DOR-001 (dependencias no identificadas, como el origen de los movimientos), DOR-002 (reglas de periodo, mes sin movimientos y fallos de generación sin definir), INV-003 (alcance poco claro: selección de mes, cuentas incluidas y contenido del PDF), BM-006 (accesibilidad no mencionada), BM-007 (comportamiento sin conexión o con error no definido) y BM-010 (regla SUGEF o validación con Cumplimiento ausente).

No encontré instrucciones incrustadas en la HU. La HU no tiene duplicados; BAN-04 también exporta a PDF, pero con otro alcance.
